_about: Coverage-class audit of the matched fragment (article §5). Each cell classifies how each of the four implementations of Table 1 covers one construction family for one lexeme group. Classifications are the author's, made by hand from the fragment's stated conditions and the sections cited in the notes; the claim counts beside each cell come from the claim register (census-normalized.json) and are not judgments. Codes: see classes. Dn marks a derivation that a separate D obtains only by admitting a determinative as the lexical head of nominal structure.

classes.D: derived by a general rule of that grammar
classes.Dn: derived by a general rule only because the grammar admits a determinative as the lexical head of Nom and NP, the structure that defines Noun in CGEL's terms; the D-noun categorization stated as a disjunction
classes.D2: derived by a rule the grammar states once for nouns and again for determinatives (or for NP and again for DP)
classes.L: a fact stored on the lexeme (a use permission, a form, a selection, an inflectional paradigm), the same in every account
classes.S: a condition stated for this construction alone
classes.U: not covered by the analysis; an attested fact left undescribed

groups.label: demonstratives, such, and the wh-forms (this, that, such, which, what)
the general quantifiers (some, all, any, both, each, either, neither, several, enough, certain, various)
the gradable four (few, many, much, little)
pronouns (she, her, it, one, who, you)
common nouns, including quantificational lot, plenty, heaps

families.label: independent argument use, including the existential
independent use with a partitive of-PP
external determination of an independent use
the compound construction: base permissions and the post-head restrictor
degree modification outside the NP; comparative complements; predicative use
predeterminer modification and the former complex determinatives
families.short: predeterminer modification and the former complex determinatives

det_use|articles.note: Det use permission and target selection (a: singular count) are lexical in every account; the phrase in Det is an NP under I1, I2, and I4 and a DP under I3 (primitives table).

det_use|every.note: as the articles; the Mod use after a genitive Det is a separate lexical permission (internal Mod family).

det_use|no_none.note: the dependent form no is selected by the Det use (forms family).

det_use|my_mine.note: a genitive NP in Det, the general realization; the my/mine form selection is lexical (forms family).

det_use|demonstratives.note: Det use permission; agreement with the target is the demonstratives' inflection (inflection family).

det_use|quantifiers.note: Det use permission with target restrictions (some: plural or non-count; each: singular count).

det_use|gradable.note: Det use permission with target restrictions (few: plural count; much: non-count).

det_use|cardinals.note: Det use with plural targets above one; complex cardinals fill Det as phrases (§5.4).

det_use|compounds.note: only as genitive NPs (someone's preferences): the general genitive-Det realization.

det_use|pronouns.note: genitive NPs (my preferences, her preferences) fill Det by the general genitive-Det realization; plain-case pronouns don't.

det_use|common.note: genitive NPs (people's preferences) by the general realization; plain-case NPs (what size shoes, Sunday morning) by a restricted construction that every account states separately.

det_use|proper.note: genitive NPs (Kim's preferences); Sunday morning is the restricted plain-case construction.

mod_use|every.note: Mod after a genitive Det (her every move): a lexical permission.

mod_use|gradable.note: the few people, her many virtues: a lexical permission for Mod use; CGEL gives few Mod after a definite determiner (p. 392).

mod_use|cardinals.note: these two hundred books, the remaining three: Mod use of cardinals.

mod_use|quantifiers.note: several, certain, various as modifiers (its several advantages): lexical.

mod_use|proper.note: Canada Day: general nominal premodification, restricted for names.

indep_arg|articles.note: no independent argument use: the lexeme lacks the use permission in every account.

indep_arg|every.note: excluded by the lexeme's permissions in every account; the corpus check is tabled in the quantifier supplement.

indep_arg|no_none.note: none as the independent form (forms family); the use is licensed by the ordinary Head chain (I1, I2) or by Det–Head fusion (I3, I4). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

indep_arg|my_mine.note: mine: ordinary Head (I1, I2) or fusion with an understood nominal (I3, I4); the agreement condition is in the agreement family.

indep_arg|demonstratives.note: independent this/that; which and what as interrogative heads. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

indep_arg|quantifiers.note: some, all, both, each, several, enough independently, and the existential There are several: ordinary Head (I1, I2) or Det–Head fusion (I3, I4). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

indep_arg|gradable.note: few and many independently, including bare few with no set under discussion (§4.2). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

indep_arg|cardinals.note: independent two, ten; the almost thirty who came is in the external-determination family. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

indep_arg|compounds.note: someone, anyone as NPs; under I3 the DP–Nom structure of Payne 2007. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

indep_arg|pronouns.note: the noun-headed NP without a determiner (She left).

indep_arg|common.note: bare plurals and non-counts; singular count arguments require determination, a condition every account states.

indep_arg|adjectives.note: the rich by adjectival Mod–Head fusion, retained in all four; bare numerous, multiple, countless are attested overlaps the article leaves unanalysed (§2.3), so a U would be right for them alone.

partitive|every.note: no partitive use (each of, not every of): lexical.

partitive|no_none.note: none of the students: the of-PP is a complement in the Nom that none heads (I1, I2); under fusion it attaches outside the DP, which the inner-phrase restriction has to state (§5.2). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

partitive|quantifiers.note: some of the wine, many of them: complement in the Nom the determinative heads (I1, I2); outside the fused DP by a stated restriction (I3, I4), §5.2. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

partitive|gradable.note: few of them, many of the delegates: as for the general quantifiers. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

partitive|cardinals.note: two of them: as above. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

partitive|common.note: a lot of the wine, a number of protesters: complement of the head noun in every account (CGEL's own analysis of a number of, pp. 351–352).

ext_det|articles.note: excluded: the permissions of independent few don't transfer to the articles (§5.2).

ext_det|gradable.note: the few, the lucky few: Det plus a Nom headed by few (I1, I2); Mod–Head fusion, the adjectival configuration (I3, I4), with the exclusion of a determiner inside the fused phrase stated among the inner-phrase restrictions (§5.2). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

ext_det|cardinals.note: the two, these three, the almost thirty who came: as for few. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

ext_det|compounds.note: excluded as determinatives by the compound construction; the set-denoting a special someone is the secondary use.

ext_det|pronouns.note: normally excluded; poor old me is a restricted case.

ext_det|proper.note: restricted in primary naming uses; the Smiths and an Ophelia are the secondary use.

ext_det|adjectives.note: the rich, the idle rich: adjectival Mod–Head fusion in all four.

int_mod|gradable.note: degree AdvPs select the gradable four (a lexical selection) and attach inside the Nom (I1, I2) or inside the DP (I3, I4); one permission covers the very few people and the very few who objected in every account. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

int_mod|cardinals.note: approximatives attach internally after an external determiner (the almost thirty who came) and peripherally otherwise (almost ten): a two-site condition every account states (§4.4).

int_mod|quantifiers.note: degree modifiers excluded for the non-gradable determinatives (very some): lexical selection.

int_mod|pronouns.note: poor old me: restricted AdjP premodification.

int_mod|adjectives.note: very tall: degree modification of adjectives.

periph_mod|every.note: almost every: NP-peripheral attachment by the general rule for peripheral modifiers, with lexical selection (I1, I2, I4); a modifier inside the DP under CGEL, so the same fact needs the DP-modifier rule beside the NP-peripheral rule that covers only you (I3), §4.4. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

periph_mod|quantifiers.note: nearly all, hardly any: as for every. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

periph_mod|no_none.note: practically no: as for every. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

periph_mod|cardinals.note: almost ten: as for every. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

periph_mod|compounds.note: hardly anyone: peripheral to the NP that anyone heads (I1, I2, I4); in DP structure under Payne 2007 (I3). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

periph_mod|pronouns.note: only you, all we who signed up: NP-peripheral in every account.

periph_mod|common.note: only the book, almost the whole class.

relative|gradable.note: few who come ever leave: an ordinary postmodifier of the Nom that few heads (I1, I2); attaches outside the fused DP, which the inner-phrase restriction states (I3, I4). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

relative|demonstratives.note: those who came, that which remains: as for few. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

relative|quantifiers.note: some that I saw: as above. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

relative|cardinals.note: two that I have seen: as above. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

relative|compounds.note: anyone who asks, something that you need to know: as above, and ordered after the restrictor (compound family). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

relative|pronouns.note: we who have read the report: a restricted range, lexical.

compound|compounds.note: the post-head restrictor's position and non-recursion, the exclusion of external determination, and the exclusion of a pre-head adjective are conditions of the compound construction in every account (§4.5); the premodifier permissions inherited from the base (hardly any, hardly anyone) are general in all four.

compound|quantifiers.note: the base supplies the compound's premodifier permissions (almost anybody from almost any): inheritance from the base in every account.

form_sel|no_none.note: inflectional forms of one lexeme selected by the use; the partitive requires none: lexical.

agreement|quantifiers.note: some of the people were: the transparency rule for quantificational heads, stated once over Nom heads (I1) or once over {N, D} heads (I2); CGEL states it for the number-transparent nouns and again for the fused-head partitive (I3); under I4 the rule for nouns covers some. each of the people takes singular agreement by default, a lexical fact in every account. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

agreement|gradable.note: many of them were; a few takes plural agreement in fused-head use: as for the general quantifiers. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

agreement|my_mine.note: Mine is ready / Mine are ready: ordinary Head needs a constructional agreement condition (§4.6); fusion takes the number from the understood nominal (I3, I4).

agreement|demonstratives.note: this/these agree with the target: the lexeme's inflection.

agreement|common.note: a lot of the work was, a lot of the people were: the number-transparent nouns (CGEL §5.3.3), in every account.

inflection|demonstratives.note: number inflection of two lexemes: lexical in every account; the paradigm parallels nominal number.

inflection|gradable.note: grade inflection (few/fewer/fewest): lexical; shared with adjectives.

inflection|cardinals.note: plural cardinals (in threes) are the secondary use (below).

inflection|common.note: count nouns inflect for number: a general rule with lexical exceptions.

inflection|proper.note: restricted number (the Smiths) is the secondary use (below).

genitive|compounds.note: everyone's, everyone else's: the head-genitive definition, 'the inflection of the head noun' (CGEL p. 479), covers a compound within Noun (I1, I4); with a separate D the definition has to be extended to D heads (I2, I3), §2.5.

genitive|common.note: dog's, the King of England's: head and phrasal genitives.

degree_outside|quantifiers.note: enough modifying adjectives, adverbs, verbs, and PPs (good enough, quickly enough): an NP modifier under the three NP-projecting implementations, under the permission that covers a great deal smaller and lots better (I1, I2, I4); a DP modifier that needs its own permission beside the NP permission (I3), §5.3. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

degree_outside|gradable.note: much bigger, a lot fewer: as for enough; the comparative complement in more than ten is licensed separately in every account (lexical), and predicative Their enemies were many is a restricted lexical fact. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

degree_outside|articles.note: the bigger the better: the as a degree modifier of comparative AdjPs, as much bigger and no better; an NP modifier (I1, I2, I4) or a DP modifier (I3). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

degree_outside|no_none.note: no better: as the bigger. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

degree_outside|common.note: a great deal smaller, lots better, heaps worse, three years old: NP modifiers of adjectives in every account (CGEL pp. 549–550).

predeterminer|quantifiers.note: all the books, both the copies: a predeterminer modifier realized by the determinative's phrase in every account (a DP in CGEL, an NP here). Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

predeterminer|gradable.note: a few, a little, a great many: an NP in Det with its own Det, as genitive Dets already are (I1, I2, I4); many a: many in predeterminer function on an a-NP. CGEL lists a few, a little, many a, and a great many as complex determinatives with a sui generis internal structure (I3), §3.1. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

predeterminer|demonstratives.note: such a mess, what a mess: degree such and exclamative what in predeterminer function (I1, I2, I4); adjectives in the same function under CGEL (I3). The difference is the category, not the machinery. Under I2 the derivation goes through the admission of D as a head of Nom and NP.

predeterminer|articles.note: a in a few, many a, such a: the article's ordinary Det use with count-singular selection (I1, I2, I4); part of a listed unit under I3.

predeterminer|common.note: half a cake, and the fractions: nouns and NPs in predeterminer function in every account (CGEL p. 385 n. 25).

secondary|compounds.note: a special someone, such an anyone, the somebodies: the secondary-use rule of §4.5, one rule over Noun (I1, I4); the same rule for nouns plus a conversion rule from D (I2, I3; CGEL p. 423 n. 43), §4.5 and §5.5.

secondary|proper.note: an Ophelia, the Smiths: CGEL's own secondary use within Noun (p. 521), the same rule in every account.

secondary|cardinals.note: in threes, in their hundreds: the same rule (I1, I4); CGEL's 'secondary use in which they inflect for number and hence belong in the noun category' is a change of category, a second rule (I2, I3), §5.5.

conditions.inner_phrase_restriction: the fused inner phrase excludes external determination, partitives, restrictors, and relatives; licensed dependents attach outside it (§5.2)
conditions.cardinal_two_sites: approximatives attach internally after an external determiner and peripherally otherwise (§4.4)
conditions.compound_restrictor: the compound's post-head restrictor: position, non-recursion, no external determination, no pre-head adjective (§4.5)
conditions.mine_agreement: agreement of independent mine with the possessed entity (§4.6)
conditions.complex_listing: a few, a little, a great many, many a listed as complex determinatives with sui generis structure (CGEL pp. 392–394)
conditions.secondary_use_rule: the set-denoting secondary use and its dependents (§4.5)
conditions.conversion_rule: conversion of a determinative to a noun for the set-denoting use (CGEL p. 423 n. 43)

duplications.peripheral_np_dp: peripheral modification stated for NP and again for DP
duplications.transparency_np_dp: number transparency stated for number-transparent nouns and again for fused-head DPs
duplications.degree_np_dp: degree modification of adjectives stated for NP modifiers and again for DP modifiers
duplications.genitive_domain: the head-genitive definition extended from Noun heads to D heads

precedence: A cell records the mechanism by which the implementation covers the licensed use. Lexical permissions, target selection, forms, and inflection are held fixed across the four implementations and are coded L only where the fact is nothing but such a permission or exclusion; where a licensed use is covered by a rule, the rule's class is recorded even though the permission is presupposed. S and D2 codes count cells; the distinct conditions and duplicated rules behind them are listed separately, since a condition stated once may apply in several cells.

sensitivity.about: The alternative coding principles of the second-round report: (1) lexical licensing takes precedence, so cells that depend on a lexeme-specific permission are L in every implementation; (2) the fused inner-phrase restriction is one general rule, so the partitive and relative cells under fusion are D; (3) a typed schema over nominal projections replaces each D2 duplication, so D2 becomes D; (4) the secondary use is a construction-specific rule in every account (already so coded); (5) the disjunctive head condition is priced at zero, so Dn becomes D.
